chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Hamza al-Thumali from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: 'Behold, the Trustworthy Spirit (Gabriel) breathed into my heart that no soul shall die until it has completed its provision. So fear Allah, Exalted and Glorious, and be diligent in seeking (it), and let not the delay of some provision cause you to seek it through disobedience to Allah. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, divided provisions among His creation as lawful (halal) and did not divide them as unlawful (haram). So whoever fears Allah and is patient, Allah will bring him his provision from its lawful source. And whoever tears aside the veil of concealment and hastens, he will take it from a non-lawful source; he will be deducted from his lawful provision, and he will be held accountable for it on the Day of Judgment.'
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim balance patience and effort in seeking their livelihood according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from the Prophet’s Farewell Sermon, this hadith establishes the theological balance between divine decree (*qismah*) and human effort (*talab*). It clarifies that while provision is pre-ordained, seeking it through sin (*ma'siyah*) does not create new wealth but rather deducts from one's allotted lawful sustenance, resulting in a dual penalty of loss and accountability.
